checks.statement: For generator g of order n≥2, {g,g⁻¹} has cardinality 2 iff n≠2.
checks.event_type: actual mathematical consistency check; mental algebra after crop c08
checks.reasoning: g=g⁻¹ iff g²=1. For g of order n≥2 this is equivalent to n dividing 2, hence n=2. Thus two-element cardinality is equivalent to n≠2.
checks.outcome: Verified under the stated order assumption. Does not decide sss/ss/ssi; no glyph supplied from this calculation.

checks.statement: The Ω→G formulation keeps two formal elements even at n=2.
checks.event_type: actual mathematical consistency check; mental algebra after second-half reading
checks.reasoning: i(a)i(b)=1 gives i(b)=i(a)⁻¹. At order 2 the generator is its own inverse, so distinct a,b may have the same image. Ω can remain two-element while its image subset collapses.
checks.outcome: Locally consistent with n≥3 restriction. This is not a proof of the full classification claim.
